newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to get tough on Third World debtors.
newsitem.headline: Russia to get tough on Third World debtors.

text.p: Russia said on Saturday it would get tough next week with some of the developing countries that owe it money when it discusses how they should repay once it joins the Paris Club of creditor nations.

"Yesterday I had negotiations with Paris Club Chairman Mr (Christian) Noyer and tomorrow with the Seven we have to make some key decisions," First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais said as he left for talks with G-7 officials in Washington.

Chubais will attend next week's meetings of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank at which he hopes to make progress with the Group of Seven leading industrial nations on Russia's bid to join the western world's exclusive clubs.
"It's the best financial elite of the world. It's on this level that we resolve the biggest issues in defence of our interests," he told Russia's NTV commercial television.

"It concerns first of all Russia's entry into the World Trade Organisation. It's also a question of the conditions according to which Russia will get back debts owed to it after joining the Paris Club," he told Russian Public Television.
Moscow, which aims to join the Paris Club as a creditor this year, hopes membership will make it easier to recover what it says are $37 billion of loans.
Most were extended to Third World countries under communism to lure them into the Soviet Union's orbit. Their exact current value is just one of many points of contention.

"There will be some big negotiations with the finance ministers of those countries which are Russia's debtors. We intend in a number of cases to toughen Russia's demands towards those countries which owe us," Chubais added.

Noyer and other Paris Club officials have said the technical obstacles in the way of Russia realising its claims "should not be overestimated". Moscow's credits were often issued on terms different to those of traditional Paris Club members.

Chubais' office said on Friday he had agreed with Noyer that the main perameters for Russian participation in the Paris Club's activities would be defined in the run-up to the June summit of leading industrial countries in Denver.
The summit has been dubbed the "summit of the eight", in a nod to Russia's desire to join the grouping, although Moscow will be excluded from some of the G-7's deliberations.
Chubais has said he does not plan to discuss Russia's IMF loan or 1997 programme in Washington but will meet World Bank officials to discuss a loan for social funding and the coal indsutry.
The IMF delayed several monthly payments on a three-year $10 billion loan to Russia because of low tax revenues, but the head of the IMF said Thursday that lending to Russia could resume next month.
